description: SPECULATRON AI is a multidisciplinary team led by a licensed Mechanical Engineer with 18 years of industrial experience. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're developing AegisμG, an AI-powered platform to analyze NASA's microgravity combustion research and advance spacecraft fire safety. We welcome innovators skilled in Python, AI/ML, data science, combustion physics, simulation, and visualization. Join us to transform scientific research into practical solutions for space exploration!
summary:
**AegisμG — Microgravity Fire Safety Intelligence**, developed by Team SPECULATRON AI, is an interactive, evidence-driven research platform designed to advance understanding of fire behavior in microgravity and support future spacecraft fire-safety research.

Addressing NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's *Flame in Freefall* challenge, AegisμG transforms NASA combustion research into accessible scientific insights through six integrated demonstrations: mission exploration, NASA evidence discovery, experimental data analysis, scientific comparison, explainable intelligence, and a digital twin sandbox.

Using NASA's BASS-II combustion report (NASA/TM-20210011385), our platform analyzes 20 PMMA combustion tests comprising 43 airflow segments, preserves missing measurements, and highlights important experimental exceptions.

Our SPECULATRON intelligence engine combines evidence-grounded retrieval, scientific comparison, research-gap identification, and DIWA provenance tracking to produce transparent, traceable insights. An educational oxygen-balance simulation illustrates hypothetical scenarios while clearly distinguishing simulations from NASA observations.

AegisμG helps researchers, engineers, students, and future mission planners explore complex combustion evidence, identify knowledge gaps, and prioritize further experiments toward safer human space exploration. It is an independent research prototype, not a validated fire-safety prediction system.
details:
AegisμG — Microgravity Fire Safety Intelligence

Team: SPECULATRON AI | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. Project Overview

AegisμG is an interactive, evidence-driven scientific intelligence platform developed for the Flame in Freefall challenge. It helps researchers explore NASA microgravity combustion experiments, compare scientific measurements, identify knowledge gaps, and investigate fire-safety questions with transparent evidence and clearly defined limitations.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity because buoyancy-driven convection is greatly reduced. This creates important challenges for spacecraft and future lunar and Martian habitats. Although NASA has conducted valuable combustion experiments, their findings are distributed across technical reports, scientific archives, and datasets that can be difficult to compare.

AegisμG addresses this challenge by transforming NASA combustion evidence into an accessible, traceable research environment.

2. How Our Application Works

Our platform provides six integrated scientific demonstration stages:

Stage 1 — NASA Evidence Explorer

Users explore NASA combustion research, identify relevant investigations, inspect scientific sources, and distinguish verified measurements from metadata-only references.

Stage 2 — BASS-II Experimental Data Atlas

The application organizes 20 PMMA combustion tests and 43 airflow segments from NASA's BASS-II Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385, Table 5.1).

It preserves 39 numerical flame-spread observations and four untracked measurements without inventing missing values. Oxygen measurements unavailable at the individual airflow-segment level remain explicitly unreported.

Stage 3 — DIWA Scientific Provenance

Our DIWA framework connects research claims to their originating sources, experimental conditions, and measurements. It distinguishes NASA observations, derived calculations, interpretations, and hypothetical model outputs.

Stage 4 — Experiment Comparator

Researchers can compare combustion experiments while examining airflow velocity, oxygen conditions, material geometry, flame-spread rates, units, and missing uncertainty information.

For example, the BASS-II M3 experiment reports flame-spread rates of 0.029 mm/s and 0.024 mm/s at successive airflow conditions of 10 cm/s and 20 cm/s. This counterexample demonstrates why scientific interpretation must consider changing experimental conditions rather than assuming that higher airflow always produces faster flame spread.

Stage 5 — SPECULATRON Scientific Intelligence

Our intelligence engine uses evidence-grounded information retrieval, scientific relevance ranking, research-gap identification, and traceable explanations.

The offline question explorer uses deterministic BM25 retrieval and can operate without an external AI API key. When evidence is insufficient, the system explicitly declines unsupported conclusions instead of generating fabricated scientific results.

Stage 6 — Digital Twin Sandbox

The platform includes an educational simulation environment that separates calculations based on reported NASA measurements from a hypothetical zero-dimensional oxygen-balance model.

Users can explore assumptions and sensitivity scenarios. Hypothetical outputs are explicitly labeled as not NASA data, not validated, and not suitable for real-world fire-safety predictions or certification.

3. Innovation and Creativity

AegisμG goes beyond conventional scientific dashboards by integrating experimental evidence, explainable intelligence, scientific provenance, research-gap mapping, and educational modeling within one interactive platform.

Our principal innovations include:

  • Evidence-first scientific intelligence: Answers are grounded in identifiable sources rather than unsupported AI-generated claims.
  • DIWA provenance framework: Research claims can be traced back to their source documents and supporting measurements.
  • Scientific integrity safeguards: Missing measurements remain missing; incompatible experimental conditions are flagged.
  • Offline research capability: Core evidence exploration and deterministic question answering operate without paid AI services.
  • Research-gap identification: The platform distinguishes measured microgravity evidence from unsupported lunar and Martian gravity extrapolations.
  • Transparent simulation boundaries: Hypothetical model results are separated from NASA experimental observations.

These features make scientific uncertainty visible rather than hiding it behind apparently precise predictions.

4. Tools, Software, and Technologies

AegisμG was developed using the following technologies:

Frontend and visualization: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts.

Backend and data processing: Node.js, Express, Zod, and PapaParse.

Scientific intelligence: Deterministic BM25 retrieval, evidence-grounded research workflows, and optional Google Gemini integration.

Development and collaboration: Google AI Studio, GitHub, Git, and AI-assisted software development using Google Gemini and ChatGPT.

Testing and quality assurance: Vitest, TypeScript checks, linting, scientific data validation, and documented source-integrity checks.

Research sources: NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), and publicly available NASA fire-protection references.

The current prototype is software-based and does not require specialized physical hardware or combustion sensors.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

AegisμG is intended to support scientists, engineers, students, educators, and future space mission researchers.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Making NASA combustion research easier to explore and understand.
  • Reducing errors caused by incompatible units, missing data, and unsupported assumptions.
  • Helping researchers identify meaningful experimental comparisons.
  • Improving scientific transparency and reproducibility.
  • Highlighting knowledge gaps that may guide future combustion experiments.
  • Supporting education and early-stage investigation of spacecraft fire-safety challenges.

Our long-term vision is to develop AegisμG into a more comprehensive research environment incorporating additional verified combustion datasets, uncertainty analysis, validated physical models, and interdisciplinary research collaboration.

6. Scientific Responsibility and Limitations

Scientific credibility is central to our design.

We recognize that experimental results from near-zero-gravity spacecraft environments cannot automatically be applied to lunar gravity (approximately 0.165 g) or Martian gravity (approximately 0.38 g).

Our current application does not provide validated predictions of spacecraft fire hazards, flame spread, smoke transport, or fire suppression effectiveness.

The educational oxygen-balance simulation is hypothetical and uncalibrated. It is not a substitute for experimental testing, validated computational fluid dynamics, or engineering certification.

AegisμG is an independent research prototype and is not endorsed or certified by NASA.

7. Conclusion

AegisμG demonstrates how open NASA research data, explainable scientific intelligence, and transparent computational tools can work together to improve access to complex microgravity combustion evidence.

By connecting research questions to verifiable observations, identifying uncertainty, and highlighting future research needs, Team SPECULATRON AI aims to contribute a practical foundation for more transparent and responsible fire-safety research supporting humanity's future in space.
